subject: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount
body:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava@borealis-sys.com>
Cc: Borealis Legal <legal@borealis-sys.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount

Team / Ava,

Quick note to request exec sign-off path for the attached proposal. Borealis is asking for two non-standard items: a one-time 25% first-year discount off list for the initial deployment and a liability cap of $1,000,000 (currently our standard is 2x MRR cap / $3M). Legal has pushed back on indemnity scope — they want a broader customer-first indemnity and to remove consequential-damage carve-outs.

Why this matters: Borealis is a strategic platform partner (pilot -> enterprise) with potential for multi-region expansion. This concession secures a 36-month SOW with expected ARR of $1.2M after year one. Revenue impact of the discount is approx $300k first-year; margin is still positive given expected uplift in year 2+ and marketplace positioning.

Requested: expedited exec clearance to accept the $1M liability cap and a limited commercial indemnity change (see redline), subject to the following conditions:
- Discount limited to year 1 and applied only to core inference service (no usage add-ons)
- Narrow data-residency carve-out: Redwood retains right to store KV-cache in our EU footprint only if requested explicitly
- Require CFO sign-off on discount finance model

Attachments: Borealis_Redline_v3.pdf, SOW-BOR-4321-v2.docx

Next step: Marissa / Lauren — can you confirm whether this is within OTE thresholds and if you want me to route to Deal Desk formally? Ava, appreciate a short note on why these clauses are critical for Borealis (so execs have context).

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Ava Reynolds <ava@borealis-sys.com>
Cc: Borealis Legal <legal@borealis-sys.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount

Karthik — thanks, looping in me and Ben to fast-track.

Commercial rationale: Borealis is committed to a multi-region launch and they've indicated they will move two pilots to paid within 9 months if latency meets SLOs. We will get the integration credited as a reference and expect an expanded ARR opportunity. We should consider this a strategic loss-leader for the region.

From a terms perspective I’m comfortable pushing $1M liability cap if Legal can narrow the indemnity to exclude third-party patent claims unless Redwood’s infra changes caused the claim. Also want warranty language limited to material defects in code we deliver for 90 days post-delivery (not ongoing fine-tuning).

Karthik — escalate to Deal Desk for CFO approval on the discount. Ben — can you run the model for FY1/FY2 impact and confirm? I want a short exec note outlining upside vs. revenue concession.

Marissa
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Borealis Legal <legal@borealis-sys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount

Karthik / Marissa / team,

Thanks for the context. Borealis can commit to the term length, but our legal team remains firm on the indemnity and warranty drafts to protect our enterprise customers. Key requests from our side (from the redline):
- Indemnity: customer requests Redwood indemnify Borealis against third-party claims arising from Redwood-delivered model outputs, including trade secret and content claims.
- Warranty: 6-month performance warranty tied to 99.5% monthly inference availability for the core API; remedy is service credits escalating by SLA tier.
- Liability cap: Borealis will not accept a cap lower than $1.2M given potential data-processing exposure.

If Redwood can accept the indemnity scope limitation (i.e., narrow to Redwood's gross negligence and willful misconduct + IP infringement caused by model artifacts that originated in Redwood codebase) and bump the liability cap to $1.2M, Borealis will sign the SOW within 10 business days.

Please advise who will provide the final signoff and whether the discount applies to trial/PO terms.

Regards,
Borealis Legal
Senior Counsel

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Reynolds <ava@borealis-sys.com>, Borealis Legal <legal@borealis-sys.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount

Marissa / Ben / Karthik — escalating to exec sign-off per process.

Summary of trade-offs:
- Revenue: 25% first-year discount ~ $300k revenue concession; expected renewal/upsell could exceed $1.5M ARR by year 3.
- Risk: Accepting $1M cap increases Redwood's net exposure for a top-tier account; bumping to $1.2M would help close, but increases expected worst-case payout.
- Legal: Borealis' indemnity language around model outputs is broader than we accept. They are willing to move to $1.2M liability cap if we accept the indemnity as proposed.

Requesting final executive decision on the following options:
A) Approve current ask: 25% year-1 discount + $1.0M liability cap + modified indemnity limited to Redwood gross negligence/willful misconduct; require CFO sign-off on discount.
B) Counter: 20% year-1 discount + $1.2M liability cap + mutual indemnity with carve-out for model-output third-party claims; require Legal escalation to produce a narrowly drafted clause.
C) Reject and hold standard terms (no discount, $3M cap) — risk losing the deal.

Please respond with option and any additional conditions. I’ll prep the deal desk note for the exec thread.

Lauren
VP, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Reynolds <ava@borealis-sys.com>, Borealis Legal <legal@borealis-sys.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Borealis: Request for executive clearance — reduced liability cap & non-standard discount

Team — decision below.

Approved: Option B with two amendments.
1) Discount: Approve up to 20% year-1 discount (not 25%). Discount must be applied only to subscription fees for the first 12 months; usage charges and professional services excluded. CFO must sign the commercial memo before SOW execution.
2) Liability & indemnity: Approve $1.2M liability cap for this customer only. Legal to draft a mutual indemnity that limits Redwood's indemnity exposure for model-output third-party claims to cases of Redwood gross negligence or willful misconduct and to IP claims where the infringement can be traced to Redwood-delivered code/model artifacts. Do not accept open-ended model-output indemnities. Warranty period: 90 days for delivered artifacts; SLA credits are acceptable up to the liability cap.

Marissa (for the Execs)
Chief Revenue Officer | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above: Borealis_Redline_v3.pdf, SOW-BOR-4321-v2.docx
